description.narrative: Strengthening Institutional and Human Resources Capacities of the Ministry of Social Solidarity Support to Covid-19 Response

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

description.narrative: - Number of villages that benefit from Takaful and Karma beneficiaries programme who receive awareness messages on Covid-19 - Number of beneficiaries reached - Number of pensioners and rural community leaders receiving their monthly stipend through e-wallet - Number of emergency operations rooms established and connected to Red Crescent - Number of volunteers mobilized - System established and promoted to connect central ministry with directorates - Number of small businesses created by NGOs through the fund - Number of direct and indirect beneficiaries from the projects - Number of employees who are registered under the social security schemes (health, social insurance, etc.) - Guidelines to respond to COVID-19 in elderly care institutions are developed and operational - Digitized system linking all elderly care institutions to central department at MOSS is up and running - Grievance center is operational - Number of PPEs and other consumables provided - Number of PWDs who access call center

comment.narrative: - Utilize existing Waai’s Good Hygiene Practices pillar to combat the spread of Covid-19, and promoting physical distancing as a protective measure, and correcting Covid-19 related misinformation and rumors, as well as Waai’s Economic Empowerment pillar for those financially impacted by Covid-19 through public announcements, also at health care centers, and pension distribution - Produce mass media and social media campaign to promote protection against COVID-19 especially among groups at risk - Set a €2 million fund to support NGOs proposals for creating local projects to meet the demands of local markets and job creation - Establish a unified registration and monitoring system for all micro-businesses funded by microcredit- supported by MoSS and support their transition to the formal banking sector - Strengthen and promote existing social insurance schemes for informal sector - Provide accessible informative materials on Covid-19 adapted to PWD, precautions and guidance through the call center - Provision of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) for employees

- Training of 114 Social Rae’edat on Wa’ai messages on several issues including hygiene and environment, precautions of CoVID 19, and the importance of vaccination. - Contracting National Center for Social and Criminological Studies (NCSCR) to develop a national observatory for socio-behavioral change and a national database for informal sector workers - Consultation meetings took place with the NCSCR to develop a conceptual action plan for implementation of signed contract to consolidate a national social observatory for socio-economic behaviors and a national database for informal sector workers - Production of “Full Stop” a short movie showing the detriments of child-marriage, and launching it in Aswan Festival for Women Cinema and furthermore, a parallel panel chaired by H.E. Minister Nivine El Kabbag, Minister of Social Solidarity on the Role of Art in affecting Social Issues and supporting CSOs to produce films documenting lessons learned on social development issues. - An actuarial study had been conducted to set a new fund to support casual workers proposed by the Ministry of Social Solidarity (MoSS) including financial and demographic projections. The results were presented to the ministerial committee on designing an integrated strategy for the social protection of informal workers and were approved. - Given the rising government prioirity to support informal sector workers (those more prone to social and economic detriments of the COVID-19 pandemic) estimated by CAPMAS to reach around 11.5 million workers, the Ministry has submitted a draft law to develop an emergency support fund for informal sector workers in times of economic crisis and natural disasters based on the findings of the actuarial study supported by the project. - Launch of MoSS social media and on-ground campaign on child marriage detrimants under the slogan “Her Marriage Before The Age Of 18 Deprives Her Of Her Rights”with an aggregate outreach of approximately 32.5 million beneficiaries. The campaign caters to support national policies condemning child marriage as a practice that violates the rights of the girl child. - National Policies supported include the issuance of a law to criminalize all forms of marriage under 18 years and furthermore, the social protection schemes of MoSS to mainstream the prevention of child marriage among the conditionalities of Takaful Program. (Child Marriage Campaign activities are co-funded with UK government) - Preparation of Request for Proposal (RFP) for NGOs to support Implementing Economic Empowerment Activities within the context of the FORSA Program Delivered by the Ministry of Social Solidarity - Implementation of MoSS campaign for combatting child marriage launched in June 2022 and ended in August 2022 through a comprehensive communication strategy including coverage in social media news networks, tv, press, national media websites, in addition to awareness raising activities on the ground. o 1,614,868 beneficiaries from Takaful Program,beneficiaries from seminars and awareness raising sessions organized by MOSS directorates in villages and districts of the 27 governorates. o 1,286,801 families benefited from door to door visits by MOSS social workers (Ra’edat). o 71,544 beneficiaries from campaign activities implemented by project contracted NGOs in 12 governorates (Cairo, Giza, Kalyobya, Matrouh, North Sinai, South Sinai, Port Said, Suez, Ismailia, Sharkia, Sohag, Qena and El Wadi El Geded) in cooperation with community development associations to ensure beneficiaries in most vulnerable villages and districts are covered by the campaign’s messages. o 25 community theatre performances by MOSS social workers (Ra’edat) during the campaign period. o CDAs contribution to the campaign - Social media campaign on different media platforms including MOSS official social media news websites, radio and TV and national newspapers and journals contracted by the project and others participating in the campaign to reflect on the commitment of Egyptian Media to the development agenda thus promoting vulnerable groups to abandon child marriage as one of the harmful practices prevalent mostly in some rural pockets and villages. o Child marriage campaign content on MoSS’s official facebook page reached an aggregate of 19 million views, with 9 million views on campaign videographs and videos (testimonials and excerpts of cinema on child marriage) and 10 million of static content of the campaign including infographs, posters, testimonials and dramatic photography posts. o 50 million views of campaign content on contracted national media websites including Sada el Balad (17 million views), Bawaba News (11 million views), El Youm El Sabe3 (15 million views) and Al Kahera 27 (7 million views). o 56 interviews of MOSS officials to present campaign content on most highly viewed radio and tv programs and channels. - Publishing of Invitation for Bidding for provision of Personal Protection Equipment (PPEs) for the social care institutions operated by NGOs and monitored by MoSS to support MoSS elderly homes in protection of residents from infection with CoVID-19. MOSS team is currently working on the PPEs distribution plan. - Launch of MoSS’s campaign for 16 days of Activism by H.E. the Minister of Social Solidarity under the title of “Hold The Thread.. And Participate In Decision Making”: o Coverage in social media, news networks, tv, press, and media websites. o Awareness raising activities on the ground implemented by MOSS directorates and social workers (Ra’edat) with special emphasis on Haya Karima villages and Takaful and Karama Beneficiairies. o Media coverage for focus group discussions with beneficiaries on different campaign issues. - The project has succssfuly procured 55,1000 antigen rapid tests through UNDP international vendors for a total value of 195,572 USD to support MoSS elderly homes in detection of COVID cases, especially in the flu season starting December 2022.
Project budget was signed as of January 2021
Project budget was signed as of January 2021

- 700 social workers and MoSS employees are trained on Waai Program Issues (Positive Parenting - Hygiene and Covid 19 Protection issues - Maternal Child Health - Early detection of disabilities - psychological support to children affected by covid 19 trauma) through trainings and workshops - 40 awareness episodes around 8-10 minutes each are aired on renowned high listenership radio networks - E-networks with MoSS directorates and key departments including Red Crescent are digitized to enhance services provided by MoSS programs - PPEs for workers for each elderly home per day (200 pair of gloves + 100 respirators) for 6 months are procured - 200 MoSS employees at helpline for PWDs are trained to respond to COVID-19 inquiries and means for protection

• The concept note and detailed plan of providing training for social workers had been completed to train them on Waai Program Issues (Positive Parenting - Hygiene and Covid 19 Protection issues - Maternal Child Health - Early detection of disabilities - psychological support to children affected by covid 19). • Manual for Training of Trainers (TOT) and stepdown training of Social Workers (Ra’edat) was developed including the pre- and post- assessment of trainers (co-funded by the Government of the United Kingdom and the European Union). • The plan of social media campaigns on highly viewed news networks and facebook is currently being prepared for enhancing social dialogue on Covid 19 detriments on socio-economic issues. • Documentation of feature stories of child marriage (Short film) for the implementation of child marriage campaign under Waai Campaign took place and the final documentary is under production (co-funded by the Government of the United Kingdom and the European Union). • Waai Comprehensive Manual covering 12 key Waai messages has developed, designed and printed to be used by social workers (Raedat), MoSS personnel, communication experts, NGO personnel etc. (co-funded by the Government of the United Kingdom and the European Union). • Child marriage booklet had been developed, designed and disseminated in Waai campaigns in 4 governorates in Upper Egypt as part of a national campaign under the auspices of the Minister of Social Solidarity. • Production of info graphs and dramatic photography on gender-based violence, highlighting success stories of empowered women who managed to overcome their discriminatory circumstances in their local communities was finalized as part of a social media campaign during the 16 days of activism against gender-based violence. • By the 8th day, the social media campaign- co-funded by the Government of the United Kingdom and the European Union- reached around 8 million persons and the official page of the Ministry of Solidarity received more than 380,000 interactions, 8,500 comments, and more than 500,000 views of the campaigns videos. Additionally, on-the ground awareness activities by Ra’edat reached more than 100,000 beneficiaries. • A concept note has been prepared for the communication campaign to extend social protection to informal workers and promote digital financial inclusion. • A national consultant was recruited to support the design and implementation of all IT related activities aiming at establishing a network of social emergency operating rooms (EOR) in all governorates hosted by the Red Crescent Association in collaboration with MoSS to immediately intervene and support marginalized groups amid Covid-19 crisis. • Criteria of beneficiaries selection and targeted governorates were finalized based on MoSS databases of beneficiaries. • An actuarial study had been conducted for a new casual workers fund proposed by Ministry of Social Solidarity (MoSS) including financial and demographic projections. • The plan of provision of personal protective equipment had been finalized according to the most updated data from MoSS database on 162 Elderly Care Institutions in 22 governorates hosting around 3,377 elderly and employing 1,100 workers. Additionally, there are 19 Homeless Shelters in 11 governorates hosting 735 persons and employing 400 workers. • Request for quotation for PPEs for elderly care institutions and homeless shelters was prepared and the process is being completed for advertisement. • A national Coordinator of the Rehabilitation Services is recruited to provide the needed supervision, implementation, organization, and follow up activities of rehabilitation services provided by MoSS to PWDs in line with the Rehabilitation Governance Strategy. • A national consultant is recruited to oversee the policy, planning, and coordination of programs for PwDs under the MOSS and Law #10 of 2018 on the rights of persons with disabilities as well as providing technical support to the Rehabilitation and Social Care of Persons with Disabilities at the Ministry of Social Solidarity (supported by the Government of the United Kingdom and the European Union). • National consultants are being recruited for the call center and grievance center supporting elderly care institutions’ and homeless shelters’ employees: TORs were prepared and being advertised.
